label: late original-phase positions (5th-8th input), boosted after l/c/x
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 99.5% of activation mass. Nearly all of it falls at orig_idx 4-7, peaking at 5-6. It never fires at t<3 or in the copy phase, and fires only weakly at the delimiter. The position window alone covers 99% of mass but only 7.6% of steps in the window are active, so position is necessary but far from sufficient. The strongest modulator is the previous input: prev_tok l gives 9.4x lift and 41% of mass, and c and x give about 2.9x each. Top activations are usually the step right after an l at position 4 or 5, and often spill over the next 1-2 steps. Sequences starting with d, t, u, m or v also raise the rate (up to 3.6x), and first occurrences of the input token fire more. Window plus prev_tok in {l,c,x} reaches dev F1 0.36 (P 0.32, R 0.41, mass recall 0.55). Adding first_tok raises mass recall to 0.81 but drops precision to 0.22. The rest seems to depend on a distributed hidden-state history that no simple predicate captures.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=l (+6.16), orig0=d (+3.04), prev2_tok=l (+2.30), orig2=f (+2.23), orig0=t (+2.21), prev_tok=c (+2.19). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-8.56), orig_idx=-1 (-6.42), prev_tok=u (-5.53), phase=2 (-4.91).
